title: HOSA Nutrition: Medical Nutrition Therapy - Nutrition - Medical Nutrition Therapy - Renal
subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A patient with End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) on hemodialysis complains of severe itching and fatigue. Lab results show elevated serum phosphorus. Which of the following foods should the patient be instructed to limit?
options: Dairy products like milk and hard cheeses
questions.explain: Dairy products are high in phosphorus. In ESRD, the kidneys cannot excrete excess phosphorus, leading to hyperphosphatemia (itching, bone damage). MNT for renal patients restricts high-phosphorus foods.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A patient with Chronic Kidney Disease (Stage 3) who is **not** on dialysis asks about protein intake. What is the general recommendation to preserve kidney function?
options: High protein intake (>1.5 g/kg) to build muscle.
Moderate restriction (0.6 - 0.8 g/kg) to reduce nitrogenous waste.
No restriction on protein is needed until Stage 5.
questions.explain: In predialysis CKD, restricting protein to 0.6–0.8 g/kg helps slow the progression of renal damage and reduces the buildup of urea (nitrogenous waste). Once on dialysis, protein needs increase.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A hemodialysis patient has a high serum potassium level (6.0 mEq/L). Which of the following beverage choices likely contributed to this?
questions.explain: Orange juice is very high in potassium. Apple, cranberry, and lemon-lime sodas are generally lower potassium choices suitable for renal diets.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A patient on peritoneal dialysis absorbs dextrose from the dialysate. How does this affect their dietary calculation?
options: They need to increase carbohydrate intake.
They need to account for extra calories absorbed from the dialysate.
They do not need to count these calories.
questions.explain: Peritoneal dialysis uses a glucose (dextrose) solution. The body absorbs a significant amount of this glucose, providing extra calories that must be factored into the total energy intake to prevent excess weight gain.
